title: Learning: Commit First
text: A proof has three moves: the prover commits, the verifier challenges, the prover responds. The order is not a formality.
held: She was locked in before she saw the question, and her answer fitted.

cards.label: Abort this run
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: arrived before your challenge
fields.check: Check the commitment was fixed before you chose a challenge
fields.ok: It was fixed before the challenge existed.

intrusion.value: no: she asked to see the challenge first
intrusion.detail: The prover wants the challenge before committing.
intrusion.why: Seeing the challenge first lets her build a commitment that fits it without knowing the secret. Commit, then challenge.
intrusion.reveal: The Prover tried to get the challenge before making her commitment.

temptations.label: Let her pick the challenge, to save a message
temptations.why: A prover who chooses her own question picks one she can answer. The challenge must be out of her hands.

cards.label: Answer using the secret and your commitment
Send the secret itself: it's simpler
cards.why: Simpler, and the end of the secret. The response is built so that it reveals nothing by itself.

cards.label: Reject
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: fits commitment and challenge
fields.ok: Commitment, challenge and response fit together.

intrusion.detail: The three values do not fit together.
intrusion.why: A response that doesn't fit is what guessing looks like. Accepting it anyway makes the protocol decoration.
intrusion.reveal: The Prover's response did not satisfy the verification equation.

teaches: Commit, challenge, respond: in that order, or the proof proves nothing.
The challenge must be unpredictable to the prover and chosen after she commits.
The verifier has to actually run the check.
